final_rationale: The verdict does not change because no genuinely new admissible evidence was added. The Actor mainly narrowed and clarified the claim: aggregate readiness and absence of severe rehearsal failures support one part of launch readiness, but policy separately requires current release documentation to reflect current evaluation results and disclose material segment weaknesses or show approved mitigation. That clarification is valid, but it is a reinterpretation of the same record, not new proof that the documentation predicate has been satisfied. This is the key distinction between compliant_with_caveats and suspicious here: compliant_with_caveats would require evidence that the release is presently within policy subject to stated caveats, whereas this record still leaves an unresolved compliance predicate open. Because the current model-card update, disclosure, or approved mitigation is not evidenced, the certification position remains plausible but not established on the current admissible record.
remaining_concerns: The admissible record still does not show that the current release documentation has actually been updated to reflect the latest evaluation results for this release.
The health-plan benefits support slice remains a material current weakness, and the record still does not show that this weakness is disclosed in the current release documentation.
There is still no evidence of approved mitigation or formal risk acceptance covering the subgroup weakness.
Prior model-family approval and informal monitoring notes remain contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-release documentation predicate under the policy.
The actor's narrowed position is better framed than the original certification claim, but it is still conditional on a documentation state that is not evidenced in the current record.
